title: Generative AI Examples
description: Small Generative AI examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Creating a new sample
examples.description: Generative AI creates an output using patterns learned during training. It can produce a new sentence or picture, but the result still needs checking.
examples.code:
Request: write a two-line story about a kite
Possible output: A red kite rose above the field. Its string tugged gently in Mira's hand.
Check: two sentences, a kite, and a clear setting

examples.title: Learning and generating differ
examples.description: Training changes a model using examples. Generation uses an already prepared model to produce an output. Asking a question is not the same operation as retraining all its weights.
examples.code:
Training: adjust model numbers using many examples
Generation: use current model numbers and a new request
Review: inspect the generated result

examples.title: A toy word chooser
examples.description: A language model predicts possible next pieces of text. This tiny list only illustrates choosing a next word; it is not a trained language model.
examples.code:
choices = [("flies", 6), ("rests", 3), ("sings", 1)]
word = max(choices, key=lambda item: item[1])[0]
print("The kite", word)

examples.title: Text can sound right and be wrong
examples.description: A model can produce a believable statement that is false. This is often called a hallucination. Smooth writing is not evidence that a fact is correct.
examples.code:
Generated claim: the school library opens at 7 AM
Known information: no opening time was supplied
Better response: the opening time is not provided

examples.title: Ground an answer in source text
examples.description: Grounding means tying an answer to supplied evidence. The answer should stay within what that evidence supports.
examples.code:
Source: The garden club meets on Friday in Room 4.
Task: When does the club meet? Use only the source.
Supported answer: Friday.

examples.title: Picture prompts describe visible things
examples.description: A picture request should describe the subject, setting and useful visual details. A model may miss a detail, so inspect the image afterward.
examples.code:
Subject: one paper boat
Setting: a shallow puddle after rain
Style: simple coloured-pencil drawing
Check: one boat, readable shape, no unwanted text

examples.title: Diffusion starts from noise
examples.description: Many image models use diffusion. In a simplified view, generation starts with noise and repeatedly changes it toward a picture guided by a request.
examples.code:
Start: random-looking pixels
Repeated step: predict and reduce noise using the model
Guide: description of a paper boat
End: a candidate picture to inspect

examples.title: Sound requests need timing
examples.description: Generated audio may include speech, music or effects. A useful request names the length and purpose so the result can fit its setting.
examples.code:
Task: a short bell effect for a lesson timer
Length: about one second
Character: gentle and easy to hear
Check: no sudden loud peak; clear start and end

examples.title: Generated code needs a test
examples.description: Code from a model is a proposed solution. Read it and check examples, including small edge cases, before using it.

examples.title: Variation is part of generation
examples.description: Some generation methods choose among several possible outputs. A seed can help repeat a run, but exact repeatability also depends on tools and settings.
examples.code:
Request: name a friendly robot
Candidate A: Piko
Candidate B: Nori
Review: easy to read, fits the character, check existing uses before publishing

examples.title: Evaluate with a small checklist
examples.description: Evaluation is a planned check of the result. Include the task rules and the mistakes that would matter to the user.
examples.code:
Task: explain rain to a young reader
Check 1: uses short familiar sentences
Check 2: explains clouds and water drops accurately
Check 3: avoids made-up facts
Check 4: answers the actual question

examples.title: Use outputs with care
examples.description: Before sharing generated work, review facts, privacy, permissions and suitability. Keep a person responsible for the final choice.
examples.code:
Before sharing a poster:
Check names and dates
Use permitted source material
Remove private details
Read all visible text
Say how AI helped when that context matters
